sketches.title: Detour Receipt
sketches.premise: Your road trip takes one wrong turn at a time, and the car keeps collecting proof of each mistake. Say what happens next as the trip gets harder to explain without anyone admitting the obvious.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the next event is caused by the current road-trip problem and adds a new piece of evidence; a skipped cause is a sudden jump, an ending is rescue or arrival, and an undo is losing, hiding, or erasing proof already on the receipt.
sketches.move_shape: Start with "Then" and add one plain event that leaves a new receipt item for the other player to use. Example: "Then the motel clerk stamps our map with the name of the town we were trying not to visit."
sketches.first_card: The driver follows a road sign that points toward the beach, but the arrow is hand-painted and slightly crooked.

sketches.title: Passenger of Honor
sketches.premise: A wrong turn makes the group pick up a stranger, animal, or awkward object that now has to come along. Keep making room for the newest passenger while the trip becomes more crowded, costly, and embarrassing.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that each next event follows from the passengers and car space already present and creates a new demand; a skipped link is a sudden new passenger or crisis, an ending is safe drop-off or a stopped trip, and an undo is removing a passenger or problem without an event causing it.
sketches.move_shape: Start with "Then" and make one event that changes who or what the car must carry. Example: "Then the goat eats the only paper map, so it becomes our navigator by chewing toward the left side."
sketches.first_card: At a tiny roadside stop, a soaked wedding guest asks for a lift to the next town.

sketches.title: Wrong-Turn Witness
sketches.premise: Every wrong turn leaves you with a witness who saw what happened and has their own version of it. Keep moving before the next witness, sign, or local makes the story harder to tell straight.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the next event is caused by the current witness and road situation and introduces a fresh fact another witness can challenge; a skipped link is an unexplained discovery, an ending is everyone agreeing or the trip reaching safety, and an undo is making a witness forget or changing an established fact.
sketches.move_shape: Start with "Then" and add one witnessed event, plainly, that gives the other player something new to dispute or build on. Example: "Then the gas-station cashier points at our bumper and says she watched us pass this same pump three times."
sketches.first_card: A cyclist at a farm gate waves you down and says your car just drove past him in the wrong direction.

sketches.title: Landmark Liars
sketches.premise: The road trip is guided by landmarks, but every landmark is described just well enough to cause the next mistake. Turn each sight into a bigger travel problem while keeping the route and its clues in play.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that each event follows from a landmark already seen and changes the route through a clear new clue; a skipped link is appearing somewhere the route has not led, an ending is finding the true destination or a final map, and an undo is declaring a landmark or route clue false after using it.
sketches.move_shape: Start with "Then" and make one event caused by the latest landmark, leaving a new landmark or route clue. Example: "Then the giant silver fish points us onto a gravel road, because its sign says the real fish is only two miles farther."
sketches.first_card: A huge painted boot stands beside the road, with an arrow aimed at a narrow lane.

sketches.title: Snack-Stop Syndicate
sketches.premise: A wrong turn turns every snack stop into a tiny deal: a favor, a trade, or a promise made to get back on the road. Keep the deals moving until the car is carrying a ridiculous chain of debts.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that each next event is caused by an existing snack-stop deal and adds one clear favor, item, or debt; a skipped link is a new bargain with no offer or need, an ending is every debt paid or the trip over, and an undo is canceling a deal or returning its cost without a new event.
sketches.move_shape: Start with "Then" and make one event that fulfills, bends, or spreads a deal while leaving a new debt for the other player. Example: "Then we trade the spare tire for six pies, so the baker sends her cousin to follow us and make sure none go missing."
sketches.first_card: At a closed fruit stand, the owner offers directions if you will deliver one box of bruised peaches.

sketches.title: The Car Knows
sketches.premise: Each wrong turn reveals a strange sign that the car itself has noticed something: a smell, a sound, a stuck window, or a dashboard warning. Treat the car like an earnest, fussy witness and follow its clues into deeper trouble.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the next event is caused by a car clue already present and makes the trip or the car’s behavior newly difficult; a skipped link is a major reveal with no warning, an ending is a repair, safe arrival, or full explanation, and an undo is making the car’s clue vanish or reversing its damage without a cause.
sketches.move_shape: Start with "Then" and add one event caused by the car’s latest clue, leaving a new clue for the other player. Example: "Then the horn blares whenever we pass a church, so the next village thinks our car is announcing a wedding."
sketches.first_card: After the first wrong turn, the dashboard begins flashing a tiny red arrow that points away from the road.
